data.name: Vola
data.long_meaning: The name Vola is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Vayu', which means wind or air. In Hindu mythology, Vayu is considered as the god of wind, and is one of the eight primary aspects of Lord Shiva. The name Vola is often given to girls born on a windy day or during a windy season.
data.spiritual_meaning: The name Vola represents the divine power of the wind, which is considered as a symbol of change, transformation, and purification in Hinduism. It is believed that the name Vola bestows the qualities of strength, courage, and adaptability upon the child.
data.numerology_meaning: The name Vola is a 5 Life Path Number, which indicates a free spirit and a love for adventure and learning. People with this number are often creative, versatile, and adaptable.

data.cultural_impact: The name Vola holds significant cultural importance in India, especially among Hindu communities. Vayu, the deity associated with this name, is an integral part of Hindu mythology and holds a revered place in Hindu rituals and beliefs. Being named after Vayu is considered a source of blessings and good fortune, as it is believed that the child will grow up to be as strong, free, and unpredictable as the winds of nature.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Vola carries deep spiritual significance in Hinduism, as it is associated with Vayu, the god of wind. Vayu is considered to be the life force that sustains all living beings, and is believed to be present in every breath we take. By giving the name Vola to a child, parents are imparting a profound spiritual connection to the natural world and the divine spirit that pervades it. It is also believed that the child will be endowed with the qualities of Vayu - strength, courage, flexibility, and adaptability - and will be able to navigate the ever-changing currents of life with grace and poise.
